subject: art-design
title: Pattern: Repeat & Symmetry
welcome_lead: From wallpaper to William Morris — how pattern repeats work.
meta_desc: KS3 pattern: repetition, motif, tessellation and symmetry.
final_note: A motif plus a rule of repeat equals pattern.

concepts.def: Repeated design or motif across a surface.
A single repeating shape or image.
Shapes that fit with no gaps or overlaps.
How a motif is duplicated across a surface.
Turning a shape around a point.

walkthroughs.body_html: Start with one motif — a leaf, a star, a face. Repeat it in a grid, half-drop or brick pattern to fill the surface. Wallpaper and fabric designers all start this way.
A tessellation tiles shapes with no gaps. Squares, triangles and hexagons tile perfectly. M.C. Escher made famous artworks using tessellating animals.
You can build pattern by reflecting (mirroring) or rotating (turning) the motif. Islamic geometric art uses rotation to make stunning star patterns.
